column8: Push the king to the edge with the queen a knight's move away, then bring your own king. Mind stalemate.
Box the king in with the rook and shrink the box; the kings in opposition push it back to the edge.
Side by side the bishops make a wall: drive the king into a corner with your king's help.
Mate only works in a corner of the bishop's color: drive the king to the edge, then walk it there with the knight's W manoeuvre.

column3: King in front on the sixth
column8: With your king on the sixth rank in front of the pawn, the pawn queens whoever is to move.
A pawn move hands the move to Black: take the opposition, then reach a key square in front of the pawn.
Stay in front of the pawn and take the opposition whenever the white king comes close.
Cut the black king off with a rook check on the d-file, then build a bridge with the rook on the fourth rank.
Keep your rook on the sixth rank; once the pawn steps forward, check the king from behind.

column3: Queen against a pawn on the seventh
column8: Black moves first. Win the pawn or mate: checks and pins make the king block its own pawn.
